children.text: Nara Smith is a lifestyle influencer who primarily posts cooking recipes from scratch and aligns her content with themes of life as a mother and wife. Joey Swoll is a fitness influencer who calls out bad gym etiquette in his reaction videos. Both Nara Smith and Joey Swoll use social norms in their content to generate engagement in different ways.

Nara Smith challenges social norms in her content, while Joey Swoll capitalizes on them. Social norms can be described as silently agreed-upon behaviors among the general public. Social norms can apply to many fields including domestic norms, manners, etiquette, etc. People tend to react negatively when these social norms are broken and these reactions can serve as a good source of content for influencers like Nara and Joey. Each of them garner attraction for their content with social norms and viewers’ reactions to breaking them in mind.

Nara's tendency to go against social norms and Joey's commentary that represents the voices of the people who follow social norms both drive engagement. In today’s social media landscape, profit from posts is driven by views, comments, and likes. Many creators will do anything they can to boost their engagement including spreading false information or saying blatantly offensive statements. This practice has come to be known as ragebait.

Both Nara Smith and Joey Swoll use more tame forms of ragebait by either bending social norms or reacting to people breaking social norms to build their platforms. Although both of these methods may not be as bad as the extreme versions of ragebait, they can still be negatives in the content creation space.
